To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the teachers' leadership strategies for technology rich upper secondary school classrooms can be captured in a four-dimensional interactive, ecological model, and that the teachers' strategies for classroom leadership can involve technical, organisational, didactic and social involvement elements.
the teachers in this study were able to create learning situations in technology-rich classrooms by means of a distributed leadership approach that involved the whole classroom community.

The leadership strategies in technology rich upper school classrooms are characterized by the use of technical, organizational, pedagogical and relational strategies, which can be understood as involving elements of distributed leadership, the classroom as collaborative community of practice and learning as knowledge creation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the teacher as a classroom leader in technology rich learning environments.
the development of leadership in upper secondary school classrooms that are technology rich and characterized by student collaboration.

the question of how leadership for learning can be conceptualized, understood and enacted in a complex and changing learning context, and how this can contribute to the development of the school as a learning community.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
leadership for learning in technology rich classrooms is a multifaceted, complex and demanding task that is best carried out by a team of teachers, and by the students themselves.

classroom leadership in technology-rich upper-secondary classrooms involves the teacher's technical, organizational, relational and didactic strategies, and that the teacher's leadership strategies can be captured in a model where the elements are interactive, and where the model can be understood in the light of a distributed leadership, a classroom as a community of practice, a collaborative, multimodal and situated learning perspective.

the findings support the view that leadership is a distributed process, that leadership is not only about technical or relational aspects, that leadership involves both didactic and organizational aspects, that the classroom is a collaborative community of practices, and that learning is a collaborative and multimodal process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

leadership for learning in technology rich upper-secondary school classrooms can be conceptualized as distributed influence, involving technical, organizational, and didactic involvement, and relational involvement, and as collaborative, multimodality and community of practice.
we have found that teachers' leadership strategies in technology-rich classrooms are complex and multi-faceted.
the leadership of learning in the technology rich classroom involves a complex interplay of technical, organizational, relational and didactic leadership strategies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

leadership for learning is not only a matter for the classroom teacher, but that the whole class community, including students, has a responsibility for creating and maintaining a learning environment that promotes learning.
the classroom leadership model we propose is not only a useful tool for teachers and teacher educators but can also be used as a basis for research on classroom leadership.
classroom leaders in upper secondary schools should be prepared to take on a more active role as facilitator of learning, rather than just being a technical expert on ICT.
